sources.title: Unreal Engine: Networking and Multiplayer

sources.applicability_note: Hub page for the networking subsystem: it links Iris, Replication Graph and dedicated-server setup rather than documenting each in depth. Used for the definition of Replication and for the existence of the subsystems, not for any numeric cost.

game_examples.fact: A shipped title with very large numbers of simultaneously animated characters, which is the workload an animation budget allocator exists to bound.
game_examples.locator: Battle-testing Unreal Engine 5.1's new systems in Fortnite
game_examples.relevance: Shows the operating condition: many animated actors, fixed frame budget.
game_examples.non_transferable: Epic develops the plugin alongside the engine; a licensee's integration and tuning cost is not represented by this example.

game_examples.fact: A cinematic-fidelity title with a small number of highly detailed characters, i.e. the opposite budget profile: quality per character rather than character count.

game_examples.relevance: Second shipped example showing the tool's budget axis being traded the other way.
game_examples.non_transferable: No animation-budget numbers are published; this shows the trade-off exists, not where the optimum is.

claims.statement: The Animation Budget Allocator is documented in the Unreal Engine documentation as a plugin that dynamically throttles skeletal mesh component animation update rates to stay inside a per-frame animation budget.
claims.locator: Documentation page: overview and budget configuration section
claims.context: Second located source for this tool. Confirms the tool is engine-documented; no throttling figures are quoted.
